title: Design: whether an accounted unadmitted change at the declared revision should keep an acceptance evaluation fresh instead of voiding it
outcome: Both coordinators (Engram and TermAl) have decided whether the unadmitted barrier ("an unadmitted change is a barrier, not a pin", commit 02ce59f, docs/features/acceptance-evaluation.md:604-615) admits a narrow relief for an accounted unadmitted change on the correct named root and generation at the explicitly declared revision, and if so the docs and the pinned tests are changed before any code
acceptance: A recorded decision by both coordinators on the narrow relief, with the contract owners named, either rejecting it or adopting the design: an accounted unadmitted observation on the correct named root and generation at the explicitly declared revision is not a basis move, its triggered obligation is exempt as the admitted branch's is, missing or unknown revisions and the wrong root or generation stay fail-closed, the bound-check unadmitted barrier and the reroll new-evidence rule are unchanged

If adopted: docs/features/acceptance-evaluation.md's unadmitted-barrier paragraph and the pinned tests (citation_sources.rs around the post-cut unadmitted change, reroll.rs around the accounted unadmitted change as new evidence) are revised first, then the code in basis_moved_after's change arm, with the test sequence Architect1 specified (a real accounted unadmitted content_comparison, the R0 to R1 sequence completing on the original evaluation id, the R2, revisionless and wrong-root variants, later-check cases, a bound-check case still blocking)
